nodes.notes: Anthropic Messages API. The prompt is assembled in 'build the pitch' so it is readable without opening this body. The model is given FACTS and told not to add any — it never sees a blank slate.

parameters.content:
## Brand deal outreach — 1 of 2: write, gate, send, log

**The job:** https://example.com/jobs/~022093291467589751915/

Northbeam, a done-for-you programme landing paid brand deals for creators. The post
hires a **person** to send 10,000+ pitches a month by hand, and rules out anyone who
"wants to build automations".

This is not an application to that post. It is the engine the post describes, built,
because their three hard gates are unusually good specifications:

> **Proven at volume** — 10,000+ pitches/month without quality dropping.
> **Deliverability literate** — warmup, domain health, spam are second nature.
> **Sharp written English** — pitches read human and personal from line one.
> Never templated.

Gates two and three are the interesting ones, because both are usually claimed and
neither is usually checkable. Here they are both **enforced in code, before a send**.

Everything you edit is in the **config** node. No environment variables.

## The personalisation gate

Facts are assembled **in code** from the brand and creator records. The model is handed
that list and told to add nothing to it. Then **audit the pitch** checks five things:

- at least `MIN_FACTS` specific details, **at least one about the brand**
- nothing from `BANNED_PHRASES` — the template tells
- inside `MIN_WORDS`..`MAX_WORDS`
- a real recipient: not a role mailbox, not suppressed
- **every number in the body traces back to a record**

That last one is the sharp end. A model that rounds 84,000 followers up to "nearly
100k" has fabricated a media kit, and the creator's name is on it.

A brand record too thin to say anything true produces **fewer facts, not a vaguer
sentence**. It is held. That is the difference between personalisation and mail-merge.

## The deliverability gate fails closed

An inbox sends only if it can be **proved** healthy — warmed past `MIN_WARMUP_DAYS`,
under `MAX_BOUNCE_RATE`, under `MAX_SPAM_RATE`, above `MIN_HEALTH_SCORE`.

`HOLD_UNKNOWN_INBOX` ships **true**: an inbox the platform will not report on is not a
healthy one. Leave it.

Two ceilings, both enforced here rather than trusted to the sending platform: per
mailbox **and per domain**. The domain one is what people forget — five mailboxes each
politely under their own cap will still cook the domain between them.

Every other mistake in cold outreach is recoverable. A burnt domain is not, and it
takes the creator's name with it.

## Same-day logging is a check, not an intention

> Log every pitch, reply and booked deal in the student's dashboard — accurate and
> same day. Careless or slow with logging: sloppy data breaks the whole system.

**Held pitches are logged too**, with the reason. A log that records only successes
cannot answer "why did we send 180 of the 400 we planned", which is the first thing
anybody asks on a Friday.

**confirm the log** compares what Airtable says it wrote against what the run produced
and reports the difference as a LOG GAP. A run that sent mail it could not log is not
a successful run that wrote a bit less.

## Nothing is sent until you say so

`TEST_RUN = true` with a blank `TEST_EMAIL` (how it ships) writes, audits and assigns
an inbox to every pitch, and sends none. Open **STOP: not sent** to read the whole
batch — the copy, the facts it was built on, the inbox, and for every held one, why.

`TEST_EMAIL` set -> pitches really are sent, all redirected to that address.
`TEST_RUN = false` goes live.

`DEMO_ROSTER` on forces preview regardless: a fabricated brand contact can never be
emailed.
